text:
emma_support: customer (AcmeMobile) reporting truncated SSE stream on /v1/generate — UI gets valid JSON up to a partial object, then stream stops, no finish_reason and no final '}' :frowning:
ingrid_se: is this the ios sdk case that was backgrounding? link to ticket: https://acme.ticket/3456
emma_support: yes — they say it repros when app goes background + token refresh happens mid-response
rajesh_eng: I pulled server logs for request id=req_9f1c. saw this sequence:
```
INFO req_9f1c stream-start client=acme mobile=iOS
WARN req_9f1c auth: ephemeral token rotated for user U-394
ERROR req_9f1c connection: websocket/sse aborted before flush: write error: broken pipe
INFO req_9f1c stream-end status=499 emitted_tokens=412 finish_reason=null
```
rajesh_eng: finish_reason is null and we emitted no final sentinel frame — that's why client sees incomplete JSON
oliver_oncall: client logs from Acme show this when reconnecting:
```
SSE_FRAGMENT: data: {"delta":"...","index":5}
SSE_FRAGMENT: data: {"delta":"...","index":6}
<socket closed>
client retries with new auth token, opens new SSE without Last-Event-ID header
```
oliver_oncall: i think the mobile SDK is reauthing and opening a fresh stream instead of resuming — server treats it as a separate request and the prior stream didn't emit the final chunk because it hit an auth rotation callback that aborted the flush
emma_support: customer is worried about corrupted JSON in the app and potential billing mismatch (they were billed for partial tokens)
rajesh_eng: repro steps I ran locally (minimal):
1) start long streaming generation via curl to /v1/generate with header `Authorization: Bearer ephemeral1`
2) midstream, call admin endpoint to rotate ephemeral token for that user (simulates auth refresh)
3) client connection receives truncated stream, server log shows 499 and no final frame
curl example:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer ephemeral1" \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=redwood-small"
```
rajesh_eng: server-side stacktrace (trimmed):
```
runtime error: write failed: stream aborted by auth-hook
at serve/sse.go:214
at auth/middleware.go:88 -> rotateEphemeralToken
```
ingrid_se: customer-side workaround: ask them to keep connection alive during token swap or use resume semantics (Last-Event-ID) until we add a server-side plan
emma_support: customer asked for a quick fix — can we add a fallback that emits a final minimal sentinel frame before auth rotation completes so clients get valid JSON?
rajesh_eng: short term: we can change auth rotation path to wait for outstanding streams to flush or mark them to emit a final 'finish' frame. need eng-release approval. risk: may delay rotation for a few hundred ms.
oliver_oncall: also noticed some clients retry immediately and concatenate fragments — recommend client enforce JSON validation and re-request completion if last chunk is incomplete
support-bot: Created ticket TKT-8891 and linked incident channel #inc-8891
emma_support: assigning to @rajesh_eng to propose mitigation, and @ingrid_se to send reproducible steps and a small failing trace to Acme engineering. i'll update the customer with the mitigation plan. :thumbsup:
